html:
The spread of horses to the peoples of the Great Plains of North America, mostly between about 1680 and 1750, which created the famous mounted bison hunting way of life.

Horses had died out in the Americas thousands of years before. The Spanish brought them back, and in New Mexico they kept them from Native people. The Pueblo Revolt of 1680 drove the Spanish out for a time and released many horses into Native trade. From there, horses passed north and east from people to people by trade and raiding.

On horseback, hunters could follow bison herds over great distances. Some farming peoples, such as the Cheyenne, left their villages for the open plains. The Comanche built a powerful trading and raiding domain in the southern plains, and the Lakota moved west to dominate the north. Wealth came to be counted in horses.

The way of life lasted little more than a century and a half. The slaughter of the bison in the 1870s and 1880s, and the reservations that followed, brought it to an end.
sum: The spread of horses to the peoples of the Great Plains of North America, mostly between about 1680 and 1750, which created the famous mounted bison hunting way of life.
